comments.body:
## RCA (Phase 1) + diagnosability fix (Phase 2 AC#3) — rebar-debug protocol

**Investigator:** Copilot CLI (rebar-debug skill), fresh worktree off origin/main @ 9532650f24.

### What is PROVEN (cited)
The incident's *shape and cost* — a 99%-then-52-min-silent job killed at the 60-min cap with
no traceback and orphaned pytest+4 workers — is caused by a **missing per-test hang guard** in
the shared reusable CI suite. `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` runs the xdist suite
(`pytest ... -n 4 --dist worksteal -q`) with **no `--timeout`** and `pytest-timeout` is not even
a declared dependency. `timeout-minutes: 60` (job-level, asserted by the existing
`test_shared_pytest_job_has_incident_timeout`) only bounds the WHOLE job, so a single test that
blocks in a C-level syscall (flock / socket recv / subprocess pipe) hides behind the last `-q`
dot and burns the full hour invisibly. This is a genuine defect against this ticket's AC#3
("whatever makes the hang diagnosable … is committed").

### Discriminating runtime proof
A minimal test that does a blocking `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)` with no timeout (the exact hang shape
suspected here), run under `-n 2 --dist worksteal`:
- **without** a guard → hangs indefinitely; an outer 25s `timeout` had to SIGKILL it (exit 124)
  — reproduces the incident's unbounded silence.
- **with** `--timeout=3 --timeout-method=thread` → aborted in **3.36s** and the culprit test is
  **named** (`… test_flock_deadlock_hangs_forever`), worker faulthandler-dumped.
`--timeout-method=thread` is load-bearing: the default `signal`/SIGALRM method cannot fire while
a worker is blocked in a C call, so it would still go silent — proven by the flock probe.

### What is NOT proven (honest)
The *specific* hanging test is **not** identified. It does not reproduce off the ubuntu/py3.11
Linux runner: I ran the CI-faithful selection locally (`-n 4 --dist worksteal`, py3.12/macOS)
under `--timeout=90 --timeout-method=thread` — 15m20s, **zero** timeout-tripped hangs (matching
this ticket's own "does not reproduce locally"). Best-evidenced candidates (unconfirmed) sit in
the network/subprocess/lock-heavy tail: `fcntl.flock` write-lock paths in `rebar._store.lock`,
tests shelling `rebar`/`git` as subprocesses, and the snapshot-fetch/review-bot drain paths.
The committed guard makes the NEXT recurrence name itself, closing AC#1 automatically.

### Fix (validated locally; RED→GREEN; held for landing)
- `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`: add `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread` to BOTH
  parallel pytest steps (default suite + integration tier). 300s dwarfs the slowest legitimate
  test; a true hang now fails in 5 min with a stack, not 60 min silent.
- `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`: declare `pytest-timeout==2.4.0` in the `dev` extra (CI installs it
  via `uv sync --locked --extra dev`).
- RED→GREEN guard test `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py::
  test_shared_pytest_suite_has_a_per_test_hang_guard`: asserts every parallel pytest step carries
  `--timeout=` AND `--timeout-method=thread`. Confirmed RED first; GREEN after; mutation check —
  removing either flag returns it to RED.

### Status
AC#3 satisfied (diagnosability instrument committed + guarded). AC#1/AC#2 require CI deployment
and will resolve on the next run/recurrence. **Not landed** — the change must go through Gerrit
(`git push gerrit HEAD:refs/for/main`); landing decision handed to the operator.

## Fix LANDED on main via Gerrit — ticket intentionally left open for AC#2

The per-test hang guard change is merged.

- **Gerrit change:** 1519 — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1519
- **Merged commit on origin/main:** f47acb7051 ("ci: add per-test hang guard to shared pytest suite"), rebased+submitted as f47acb705190bdfc9f3660f6ee55c70e1bb655d8.
- **Gates:** Verified +1 AND LLM-Review +1 (rebar review bot), no unresolved comments; submitted by plain Gerrit Submit (Rebase-If-Necessary, no pre-rebase needed).
- **CI run:** https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/31217402209 (green; Actions responsive despite the 2026-08-06/07 outage window).
- **Content:** `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread` added to both parallel pytest steps in _build-and-test.yml; `pytest-timeout==2.4.0` declared in the dev extra + uv.lock; parity guard test test_shared_pytest_suite_has_a_per_test_hang_guard.

### Pre-land durations sanity check (per-test bound is 300s)
Ran the CI-faithful default selection locally (`-n 4 --dist worksteal --durations=25 --timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread`). No test tripped the 300s guard. Slowest single tests: test_pass_lock_blocks_before_fetcher 124.0s and test_a_missing_epic_field_aborts_provisioning 120.3s — both comfortably under the ~180s advisory line and well under 300s. (Local parallel git-store flock contention produced unrelated failures/errors that pass serially; none were timeout trips.) Guard is safe; no legitimate test is near the bound.

### Remaining before close
- **AC#1** (name the hanging test): resolves automatically on the next recurrence, which the committed guard will now name.
- **AC#2** (ubuntu py3.11 cell completes within 60 min on **three consecutive Verified runs** post-merge): OUTSTANDING — needs three green post-merge Verified runs observed. **Leaving this ticket in_progress until AC#1/AC#2 are met.**

Scope note: external-lane follow-up d835-1846-95d1-4d84 left untouched for its owner.

# The `Verified` gate's `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.11)` cell hangs after ~99% of the suite and is cancelled at the 60-minute job timeout

## Symptom

The cell prints progress normally for ~10 minutes, reaches `[ 99%]` with **zero** `F`/`E`
markers, and then emits nothing at all until GitHub kills it:

    2026-08-07T17:04:16.9396830Z ....................................... [ 99%]
    2026-08-07T17:55:12.0420609Z ##[error]The operation was canceled.

`timeout-minutes: 60` is set on the `test` job in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`.
The CI bot reads the cancellation as a failure and votes `Verified -1` + `Code-Review -1`,
so an otherwise-green change cannot land.

## Not change-specific

Seen on at least two unrelated changes on 2026-08-07:

* change 1505 (`9fb3`), three consecutive runs — 31194624887, 31199714760, 31206898501 —
  including one run **after** a rebase onto `origin/main` @ 9532650f24.
* run 31208164115, a different change, same signature: `[ 99%]` then
  `The operation was canceled.`

The other matrix cells (ubuntu py3.12, ubuntu py3.13, macos py3.13) complete the same
selection in 11-21 minutes on those same runs, so it is specific to the ubuntu/py3.11 cell.

Counting the progress dots on run 31199714760's cell: 11160 of ~11215 tests had reported
before the silence, so roughly the last ~55 tests are where it stalls. It is a hang in the
test tail, not in coverage combining or teardown after the run.

## Does not reproduce locally

On macOS with the CI-faithful configuration — `uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra
reviewbot --extra ui --python 3.11`, then `REBAR_REQUIRE_EXTRAS=1 pytest -m "not
integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q -p no:cacheprovider --durations=25
--cov=rebar` — the suite finishes in 15:00 with 11196 passed, 19 skipped, exit 0. So the
trigger involves the Linux runner (4 vCPU, `fcntl.flock`-backed store locking) rather than
the interpreter version alone.

## Why it matters

Every change in flight can be blocked by a red `Verified` that reflects no real defect, and
the only workaround is to keep posting `recheck` until a run happens to get through. That is
the same class of problem as a gating advisory failure: the gate stops discriminating.

## Suggested first moves

- Add `-v` (or `--timeout` via `pytest-timeout`) to the ubuntu cells so the hanging test
  names itself instead of being invisible behind `-q` dots.
- Suspect first the store's write-lock paths (`fcntl.flock` + `mkdir`) and any test that
  shells out to `rebar` as a subprocess, since a blocked lock acquire is the shape that
  produces exactly this silence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the hanging test (or the blocking call) is named, with a CI log line or a local
      reproduction showing it stalled
- [ ] the ubuntu py3.11 cell completes within the 60-minute job timeout on three
      consecutive Verified runs
- [ ] whatever makes the hang diagnosable (a per-test timeout, `-v`, or a faulthandler
      dump) is committed, so a recurrence names itself instead of going silent
